- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.17) over 3+ consecutive days, model may overfit upward trend; apply mild downward bias (–0.5 to –1.5%) to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day avg, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.22 or -0.61) followed by recovery, model often fails to adjust; forecast should lag 1–2 days behind true trend in such cases.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (by > 2% over 5+ days), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
